title: Anock
summary: Anock is an Indigenous place name connected with a short creek at the bottom of Fourth Neck in the East Quogue area of Southampton, historically called Atlanticville. It is close to, but distinct from, the nearby Weesuck place name.
address_label: General southern Fourth Neck / East Quogue creek area, Southampton, NY
why_this_matters: Anock preserves a Native creek name in the East Quogue area, even though no settled translation has been found. Its short form shows how Indigenous names could be compressed or altered in English records while still pointing to specific waterways and necks of land. The South Fork landscape was shaped by Native language, movement, and memory before later town and property names took hold.
translation_content:
The recorded forms are Anock and Annock. No reliable translation is given in the available source; the name may preserve only part of a longer Algonquian-language word whose full form cannot be recovered from the surviving written forms.

Why Place Names Matter

“Mountains come with stories; names are tangled with meaning. Indigenous place names carry physical descriptions, information about resources, stories both practical and sacred.”

— Sacred Lands Conservancy with Tah-Mahs Ellie Kinley, The Many Faces of a Mountain: Sharing Importance and Meaning Behind Indigenous Place Names (2024), ‘Mountains Come with Stories’ section
whereintheworld_content: Anock adds detail to the Fourth Neck landscape by preserving a smaller creek name that could otherwise be folded into better-known nearby places. It also shows how fragmentary records can still help map older Indigenous placename geography when uncertainty is made clear.
